subtopics.title: The Scale from Impossible to Certain

questions.question: The probability scale runs from:
options: 0 for impossible to 1 for certain, with nothing beyond either end

questions.question: A wheel with ten equal sectors, one marked WIN, gives a winning probability of:
An 'event' differs from an 'outcome' because an event:
options: Is the set of outcomes you care about — 'greater than four' bundles 5 and 6

questions.question: If the wheel wins with probability one tenth, it loses with probability:
options: Nine tenths — the two must total exactly 1

questions.question: The minibus arrived full on 18 of 50 mornings. The relative frequency of a full minibus is:
Minibuses, weather and power cuts need relative frequency rather than theoretical probability because:
options: They own no symmetry — their chances must be estimated by watching
Theoretical probability only works for large numbers

questions.question: Eight heads in ten flips of a fair coin means:
options: The theoretical probability has changed to 0,8
Nothing alarming — tiny samples wobble; a thousand flips at that rate would be evidence
The next flips must be tails

questions.question: A coin flipped 250 times gives 110 heads. The full-marks comparison says:
options: The coin is unfair because 110 is not 125
Theoretical 0,5, relative frequency 0,44 — close together, so the coin behaves fairly over a respectable test

subtopics.title: Tree Diagrams: Chance in Two Steps

questions.question: Tossing a coin twice produces the equally likely combined outcomes:
options: Heads-heads, heads-tails, tails-heads, tails-tails — four journeys
Two heads or two tails only

questions.question: The probability of exactly one tail in two tosses is:
options: A half — the two journeys heads-tails and tails-heads

questions.question: The rule for combining probabilities along a tree's branches is:
options: Subtract the smaller from the larger
Multiply along the journey — a half times a half gives each coin path a quarter

questions.question: If the food stand runs out of boerewors rolls with probability 0,1 each day, independently, then rolls available two days running has probability:

subtopics.title: Two-Way Tables: Chance in a Grid

questions.question: With 36 learner-minibus, 54 learner-walk, 24 adult-minibus and 36 adult-walk, the totals are:
options: 90 learners, 60 adults, 60 by minibus, 90 walked, 150 in all

questions.question: The probability that a random visitor is an adult who came by minibus is:
options: The single cell 24 over the grand total 150 — 0,16

questions.question: 'Given that a visitor is a learner, the chance they came by minibus' is:
options: 36 over 90 = 0,4 — the words shrink the world to the 90 learners

questions.question: Choosing the denominator in a two-way-table question depends on:
options: The wording — grand total for 'a random visitor', a row or column total when the question says 'given' or 'of the learners'

questions.question: One half, 0,5 and 50% are:
options: The same chance in three languages — fraction, decimal and percent
Increasingly likely versions of the same event

questions.question: Drawing a red sweet blind from a bag of 4 red and 16 green has probability:
An answer of 1,3 for a probability is:
options: Acceptable if the working is shown
Broken — nothing outranks certainty, so no probability exceeds 1

subtopics.title: The Minibus You Watched for Fifty Mornings

questions.question: The minibus's chance had to be watched rather than calculated because:
options: There is no rulebook of symmetry for minibuses — real-world chances are measured by counting
Counting was easier than the formula
Coins are more reliable than timetables

questions.question: Fifty mornings of watching beats five mornings because:
options: The longer you watch, the closer the count creeps to the truth
Five mornings would give probability zero
The minibus changes route after five days

questions.question: Karabo's estimate of 0,36 for a full minibus means roughly:
options: The minibus is full every third week
A thirty-six percent risk of watching a full minibus drive past on any school morning

subtopics.title: Branches and Grids: Handling Two Things at Once

questions.question: The tree diagram exists mainly to:
options: Lay every journey in front of your eyes, catching the route head-jugglers lose — like tails-heads

questions.question: The picture for a crowd where each person wears two labels is:
options: The two-way grid, with cells and totals that must agree

questions.question: When rows and columns of the grid refuse to add to their totals:
options: The grand total should be changed
A cell is lying, and catching it before answering costs nothing

questions.question: Seeing 'given that' or 'of the learners' in a question means:
options: Add the row and column totals
The denominator stops being 150 and becomes the named group's total
